s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic headache disorder with postural exacerbation
salient_findings: Inferior displacement of the cerebellar tonsils on MRI
Ventral cervicothoracic epidural CSF collection on CTM
key_facts: 10-year history of headaches
Medical history significant for migraine
Headaches worsen upon standing
MRI Head showed inferior displacement of the cerebellar tonsils
CTM showed extradural contrast spread at multiple cervical and thoracic levels
Ventral cervicothoracic epidural CSF collection extending from mid cervical spine to mid thoracic level
No specific physical examination findings were reported
Patient is a 25-year-old female

shortlist.label: Chiari malformation type I
shortlist.why_kept: Inferior displacement of cerebellar tonsils on MRI Head

shortlist.label: Spontaneous intracranial hypotension
shortlist.why_kept: Headaches worsen upon standing and extradural contrast spread on CTM

shortlist.label: Syringomyelia
shortlist.why_kept: Ventral cervicothoracic epidural CSF collection on CTM

shortlist.label: Cerebrospinal fluid leak
shortlist.why_kept: Extradural contrast spread at multiple cervical and thoracic levels on CTM

shortlist.label: Pseudomeningocele
shortlist.why_kept: Ventral cervicothoracic epidural CSF collection extending from mid cervical spine to mid thoracic level

raw.rationale: Worsening headaches upon standing and evidence of extradural contrast spread and ventral cervicothoracic epidural CSF collection suggest a CSF leak, which is more consistent with spontaneous intracranial hypotension
raw.anchor_refutation: Chiari malformation type I does not typically cause worsening headaches upon standing or CSF leaks, and the imaging findings are more suggestive of a CSF leak than a Chiari malformation

rejected.label: Chiari malformation type I
rejected.why: Imaging findings and worsening headaches upon standing are not typical for Chiari malformation type I

rejected.label: Syringomyelia
rejected.why: No evidence of a syrinx in the spinal cord on imaging

rejected.label: Cerebrospinal fluid leak
rejected.why: Too broad, as spontaneous intracranial hypotension is a more specific diagnosis that explains the patient's symptoms and imaging findings

rejected.label: Pseudomeningocele
rejected.why: Not directly related to the patient's symptoms and imaging findings, which suggest a CSF leak and intracranial hypotension
